the use of a cascade classifier for the classification of breast lesions on dynamic contrast enhanced MR images is more accurate than a one shot classifier and that the use of separate feature selection and training for mass and non mass lesions further improves the classification accuracy.
the use of a cascaded classifier improves the performance of a CAD system for differentiating between mass and nonmass enhancing breast lesions during dynamic contrast material-enhanced MR imaging.

we propose a novel two stage classification approach to improve the diagnostic performance of CAD for breast MRI, and we achieve a significant improvement in the diagnostic performance of a CAD for breast MR by using a two stage classification approach compared to a one shot classification approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an automatic CAD system to differentiate between mass and non-mass enhancements in breast MR imaging.
the design of an automatic system that can detect and classify breast lesions in MR images.
the development of a computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) tool to improve the detection and characterization of breast cancer on magnetic resonance (MR).
